item.title: Benn Jordan Testifies on Flock Safety ALPR Surveillance
item.description:
Benn Jordan Testifies on Flock Safety ALPR Surveillance

Benn Jordan, musician‑turned‑investigative journalist, has become a leading voice exposing the private‑sector surveillance network built around Flock Safety’s automatic license‑plate readers (ALPRs).

🔎 Overview

  • Jordan has shifted from an experimental music career to investigating Flock Safety’s ALPR systems.
  • His work has prompted congressional testimony, government scrutiny, and contract cancellations.

🎤 Who is Benn Jordan

  • Musician, YouTuber, researcher, and investigative journalist.
  • Known for a prolific discography of experimental music dating back decades.
  • In the last couple of years, he has become a high‑profile face in creator and media spaces for his work investigating Flock Safety.

📡 Flock Safety’s ALPR Network

  • Flock manufactures automatic license‑plate readers and the software that powers them.
  • Atlanta has more Flock cameras than anywhere else per square mile.
  • Jordan first noticed the cameras about two years ago, initially thinking they were traffic cameras.

🏛️ Congressional Testimony and Political Response

  • Jordan recently testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism on Flock and other ALPR systems.
  • Hundreds of cities, counties, and other local governments have begun canceling contracts with Flock.
  • Republican Senator Josh Hawley has opened an investigation into Flock.

📉 Business Impact

  • Reuters reported that Flock plans to cut about 18 percent of its workforce.

🛠️ Jordan’s Accountability Approach

  • He does not hate Flock as a company; he says its posture toward critics is a PR failure.
  • He talks directly to Flock’s CEO Garrett Langley and reports security vulnerabilities when he finds them.
  • His YouTube videos and collaborations with other researchers, civil‑rights groups, and journalists serve as an accountability function that forces the conversation to the forefront.

📢 Why It Matters

  • The issue extends beyond Flock to the interlocking relationship between private industry, government, and law enforcement that prioritizes secrecy over transparency.
  • Lack of transparency allows a network of cameras to be deployed without public consent, raising concerns about abuse by police officers.
  • Jordan emphasizes that society never voted for an insecure network of cameras on every street corner.

#Surveillance #Privacy #ALPR #Congress #FlockSafety

Source: Benn Jordan thinks the surveillance problem is much bigger than Flock

item.title: Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore Deploy On‑Device AI Scam Detector
item.description:
Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore Deploy On‑Device AI Scam Detector

Google DeepMind and Singapore’s Government Technology Agency (GovTech) have jointly released a privacy‑preserving, on‑device scam detection model as part of the National AI Partnership.

🔍 Overview

  • The model is fine‑tuned on local scam conversations and runs entirely on the user’s device.
  • It aims to protect citizens from complex social‑engineering scams while keeping conversation data private.

📈 Problem Landscape

  • Scams such as investment fraud, fake job offers, and impersonation of public officials make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes.
  • These scams have caused more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019 and account for up to 80 % of all loss amounts.
  • Attackers have shifted from simple phishing to elaborate social‑engineering tactics that involve convincing conversations before requesting money.

🤝 Collaboration

  • Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore are collaborating under the National AI Partnership with the Singapore Government.
  • Development was performed inside GovTech Singapore’s managed GCP environment (a “Sovereign Sandbox”).
  • Training data excluded private or personally identifiable information and used anonymised scam‑report and intelligence feeds.

🛡️ How the On‑Device Model Works

  • Two‑stage pipeline:
    1. Stage 1 – a lightweight, efficient classifier screens inbound messages with minimal power consumption.
    2. Stage 2 – an in‑context analysis using the fine‑tuned Gemma model examines a larger snapshot of the conversation to confirm a threat or dismiss a false alarm.
  • When a manipulative conversational pattern is detected, a real‑time warning appears on the device, prompting the user to pause and verify before sharing sensitive information or funds.
  • The model processes conversation data only on the device, with user consent, and neither Google nor the Singapore Government can access the user’s messages.

⚙️ Technical Details

  • The lightweight Gemma model was fine‑tuned on local scam dialogues, including impersonations of public institutions, banks, local figures, and trending regional schemes.
  • Generic models often struggle with local deception techniques; the fine‑tuned model can distinguish benign social chatter from genuine manipulation.
  • Stress‑testing involved synthetic dialogues and local corpora to cover diverse scam categories and evolving impersonation tactics.

🚀 Deployment & Availability

  • The rollout will be carefully phased and developed in partnership with the Singapore Government.
  • Integration into applications will allow faster analysis of conversation patterns and help citizens act before financial or credential exposure occurs.
  • The collaboration was presented at Singapore International Cyber Week (SICW 2026) as a model for messaging platforms that balance user protection with end‑to‑end encryption.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Demonstrates how AI can counter criminal activity without compromising safety or privacy.
  • Provides a concrete example of local, real‑time scam detection while preserving the confidentiality of chat interactions.
  • Sets a precedent for future AI‑driven security solutions that respect sovereign data governance.

#AI #ScamDetection #Privacy #Singapore

Source: On-Device AI Against Scams: Google DeepMind & MDDI

item.title: ONE Data Launches Development Finance Observatory AI Platform
item.description:
ONE Data Launches Development Finance Observatory AI Platform

ONE Data, an initiative of the ONE Campaign, launched the Development Finance Observatory on October 14, 2026 during the World Bank‑IMF Annual Meetings. The AI platform is supported by The Rockefeller Foundation and Google.org and aims to give free, rapid access to global aid, lending and debt data.

🔍 Overview

  • The Development Finance Observatory is an AI‑powered data analyst that brings together fragmented development finance data in one place.
  • It is described as “a world‑class data analyst in your pocket.”
  • The platform is built on Google’s Data Commons and supported by the Rockefeller Foundation’s independent charitable affiliate RF Catalytic Capital (RFCC).

🧩 How it works

  • The platform unifies isolated datasets—from the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, Organisation for Economic Co‑operation and Development, and other sources—into a single AI‑ready foundation.
  • Users can query the data with natural‑language questions instead of navigating raw spreadsheets, turning analyses that previously took months into minutes.
  • Every number is traceable to a specific source, preventing AI‑hallucinations.
  • Calculations and visualizations that used to take months now take minutes.

⚙️ Key details

  • Launch date: October 14, 2026, Washington, D.C.
  • Funding: $4 million in combined funding from ONE Data, Google.org and The Rockefeller Foundation (announced in January).
  • Technology partner: Built on Data Commons by Google with support from RFCC.
  • Initiative: Part of ONE Data, which “transforms fragmented, inaccessible development data into trusted, actionable insights for policymakers, campaigners, journalists, and citizens.”

🚀 Availability

  • The platform is publicly available, offering free, rapid access to aid, lending and debt data for governments, journalists, think tanks and the public.
  • Users can ask natural‑language questions and receive answers in seconds with confidence that the answers are correct.

💡 Why it matters

  • The observatory gives leaders a clearer picture of aid, debt, private capital and other financial flows, enabling faster, smarter decisions about where limited resources can have the greatest impact.
  • As the development finance landscape is “being rewritten in real time,” transparent, accountable data is essential for building a more effective system.
  • Quotes from stakeholders:

    “We believe policy makers — who make decisions that impact millions of people’s lives– deserve world class insights.” said David McNair, Managing Director of ONE Data. “We built the Development Finance Observatory so that policymakers, journalists and citizens can get the answers they need in seconds — with the confidence that those answers are right. “Data Commons was built so organizations like ONE can focus on solving the world’s biggest challenges without worrying about data storage and APIs,” Prem Ramaswami, Head of Google Data Commons, said. “The development finance landscape is being rewritten in real time, and we cannot build a better system without understanding how money is actually moving,” said Mike Muldoon, Chief Executive Officer of RFCC, The Rockefeller Foundation’s independent charitable affiliate.

#developmentfinance #AI #dataanalytics #publicpolicy

Source: ONE Data Launches AI Platform That Transforms International Development Sector

item.title: US House to Vote on Bipartisan Bill Protecting Households from Data Center Power Costs
item.description:
US House to Vote on Bipartisan Bill Protecting Households from Data Center Power Costs

The US House of Representatives is expected to vote on the bipartisan ‘Ratepayer Protection Act’ this Wednesday. The legislation aims to prevent the soaring costs associated with data center expansion and power needs from being passed on to average household electricity bills.

🔍 Overview

Introduced by Representative Kathy Castor (D-FL) and Representative Gabe Evans (R-CO), the bill seeks to ensure that large data centers pay their fair share of the costs for expanding the electricity grid. The proposal comes as government officials face pressure to manage the increasing energy demands of the AI industry while protecting consumer affordability and grid reliability.

🧩 How it works

  • Cost Allocation: State utility regulators would be required to consider whether large electricity users should pay for the infrastructure needed to serve them.
  • Capacity Threshold: The proposed rules would require new data centers using at least 20 megawatts to cover the additional power infrastructure costs they create.
  • Rate Reductions: Regulators would have the authority to charge large data centers extra to help lower the bills of other utility customers.
  • State Authority: The bill would give states more freedom to impose conditions, such as requiring data centers to secure new power supplies or placing limits on their electricity usage.

⚙️ Key details

The following reactions and perspectives have been reported regarding the proposed legislation:

Entity or Individual Position Perspective
Hakeem Jeffries House Democratic Leader Called the proposal an ‘appropriate step forward’ but noted ‘more clearly needs to be done.’
Allison Clements Former FERC member Described the bill as a ‘modest step in the right direction’ that signals congressional alignment on protecting customers.
Craig Sundstrom Amazon Energy Policy Director Stated the bill ‘could unlock the investment needed to build new generation and transmission faster.’
Ari Peskoe Harvard Electricity Law Initiative Highlighted that no other industry’s electricity usage has captured so much political attention.
Technology Industry Official (Via Axios) Described certain provisions as an ‘unprecedented level of discriminatory treatment’ for a single industry.

💡 Why it matters

While data centers have existed for decades, the growth of AI has significantly increased the demand for new power plants and grid upgrades. This shift has raised concerns regarding higher costs for households. The bipartisan support for the bill arrives ahead of the November midterm elections, highlighting the political priority of grid reliability and consumer costs. While Amazon suggests the bill could accelerate infrastructure investment, the Data Center Coalition is currently reviewing the legislation. Microsoft, Google, and Nvidia declined to comment, while Meta did not respond to requests for comment.

#DataCenters #EnergyPolicy #ArtificialIntelligence #Legislation

Source: US moves to stop AI data centres from pushing up household electricity bills. Here’s what could change for Americans

item.title: World Bank Update Highlights AI Growth and Policy Needs in India
item.description:
World Bank Update Highlights AI Growth and Policy Needs in India

The World Bank released its India Development Update, highlighting AI as a key development opportunity for the country.

📈 Economic Context

  • India’s economy is projected to grow at 7.1% in FY27 supported by robust domestic demand and strong exports, despite global headwinds.
  • It remains one of the fastest‑growing major economies and a key contributor to global growth, according to the World Bank’s latest economic update.
  • The South Asia Economic Update projects regional growth of 6.9% in 2026, keeping South Asia the strongest‑growing region.

🤖 AI Investment and Workforce Trends

  • Private AI investment rose three‑fold, from $1.2 billion in 2024 to $4.1 billion in 2025.
  • Global Capability Centers (GCCs) employed 1.9 million professionals in 2024, increasing to 2.36 million in 2025.
  • India is listed among the top 10 emerging‑market performers on AI readiness.

🛠️ Policy Recommendations

  • The Update calls for cross‑cutting actions to deepen AI‑enabling infrastructure, improve the business environment, broaden AI access, and enhance labor capacity so benefits are broadly shared.
  • Recommended measures include:
    • Strengthening workforce skills.
    • Establishing a more business‑enabling environment.
    • Improving physical and digital infrastructure.
    • Reducing barriers for small firms, fostering local AI innovation, and creating a clear regulatory framework that safeguards data security and privacy.

🌾 Small AI for Development

  • The report stresses that AI should be used as a development tool, not just a technology, to boost productivity and improve public services.
  • Through AgriConnect, the World Bank Group is investing in ‘small AI’: targeted, locally‑adapted tools that ensure gains are accessible and widely shared while supporting workers through the transition.

🌏 Regional Perspective

  • For most of South Asia, the greatest gains lie in adopting AI and adapting it to local conditions, including small AI applications suited to low‑resource settings.
  • “The adoption of AI has the potential to transform South Asia’s development trajectory by boosting labor productivity, expanding export opportunities, and improving public service delivery. But to reap these benefits, governments need to address the foundational gaps that hold back adoption.” – Franziska Ohnsorge, World Bank Group Chief Economist for Asia
  • “India is one of the top 10 leading emerging-market performers on AI readiness**.” – Paul Procee, World Bank Acting Country Director for India

⚠️ External Risks

  • The Update notes elevated external risks, including downside risks from global oil prices, El Niño, and stock‑market corrections that could cause capital‑flow volatility.

#IndiaAI #WorldBank #EconomicDevelopment #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: India’s Growth Intact Despite Global Headwinds; AI Can Create New Opportunities through Policy Actions

item.title: Sen. Schiff pushes for AI regulatory agency amid White House non‑binding pledge
item.description:
Sen. Schiff pushes for AI regulatory agency amid White House non‑binding pledge

In 2026, Senator Adam Schiff highlighted a growing push for federal regulation of artificial intelligence, citing recent White House events and a Supreme Court decision that could shape any new AI agency.

🔍 Overview

  • President Donald Trump gathered AI CEOs at the White House to sign a non‑binding pact agreeing to keep AI safe.
  • A separate group of tech executives signed a voluntary pledge to evaluate their own AI systems.
  • Schiff, a Democrat from California, opened the conversation by discussing self‑dealing and corruption in politics.
  • He emphasized the need for regulation rather than relying solely on industry promises.

🏛️ Legal backdrop

  • The Supreme Court case Loper Bright overturned a Reagan‑era precedent that gave agencies deference when laws were vague (Chevron deference).
  • Courts now decide on such matters, which could cause any new AI regulation to become entangled in litigation.

⚙️ Proposed regulatory approach

  • Schiff supports creating a new agency to regulate AI.
  • He noted that the Supreme Court decision makes immediate litigation a real risk for new regulations.

🚨 National security concerns

  • Advanced models, especially those that improve themselves recursively, reduce our ability to understand their decisions.
  • The Pentagon’s unbridled AI use could lead to calamities; there is a call to investigate AI’s role in the bombing of an Iranian girls’ school.
  • Anthropic has refused to use AI for domestic mass surveillance or fully autonomous weapons, prompting an administration effort to “kill” the company.
  • When asked about these concerns, the president answered that the world need not worry because “these companies love America.”

📣 Why it matters

  • The combination of industry self‑regulation, a potential new federal agency, and a Supreme Court shift creates a complex landscape for AI governance.
  • National security implications add urgency to establishing clear, enforceable rules.

#AIRegulation #SenSchiff #NationalSecurity #SupremeCourt

Source: Sen. Adam Schiff on making Congress relevant in the AI age

item.title: Former New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Cites AI Analysis to Dispute Harassment Investigation Findings
item.description:
Former New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Cites AI Analysis to Dispute Harassment Investigation Findings

Former New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell is using outputs from artificial intelligence to challenge the results of an investigation that led to his resignation. Following his departure on September 25th, which occurred after an investigation found he had sexually harassed a staffer and violated ethics rules, Caldwell has claimed that multiple AI agents support his assertion of innocence.

🔍 Overview

  • Dale Caldwell resigned on September 25th following findings of sexual harassment and repeated ethics violations.
  • The former lieutenant governor has engaged in media appearances, including an interview on NJ PBS with host Rob Nelson, to clear his name.
  • Caldwell argues that he is being unfairly targeted and asserts that multiple AI platforms back his position.

🧩 How it works

Caldwell reported using various AI tools to evaluate the investigation’s findings:

  • He processed the report through multiple AI platforms, a process he described as having “AIed” the document.
  • During his NJ PBS interview, he stated that he submitted the report to AI 59 times.
  • For each submission, he asked the AI, “What would your findings be?”

⚙️ Key details

  • Caldwell claims that in every instance, the AIs failed to find that sexual harassment occurred.
  • Observations regarding the behavior of AI chatbots suggest they are notoriously sycophantic and frequently provide users with the information they want to hear.
  • It is noted as highly unlikely that Caldwell would have wanted the AI to confirm findings that he engaged in sexual harassment.

#DaleCaldwell #ArtificialIntelligence #NJPolitics

Source: NJ’s lieutenant governor resigned over a sexual harassment investigation, but insists AI says he’s innocent.

item.title: Congress Debates Legislative Solutions for Rising AI Data Center Electricity Costs
item.description:
Congress Debates Legislative Solutions for Rising AI Data Center Electricity Costs

Congress is scrambling to address voter concerns over the impact of AI data centers on residential electricity rates as lawmakers debate new legislative measures. With the data center industry rapidly expanding, regional utilities are building tens to hundreds of millions of dollars in new infrastructure, raising questions about how much of these costs will be passed on to everyday utility customers.

⚖️ Legislative Initiatives

Several data center and AI-related bills are moving through Congress. The primary competing measures include:

Bill Name Sponsor / Promoter Key Provisions & Status
Ratepayer Protection Act Sponsored by Ohio Republican Sen. Jon Husted Would have state utilities consider holding “large-load” customers responsible for increased costs. Passed the House in September with strong bipartisan support; opposed by Senate Minority Leader Sen. Chuck Schumer.
GRID Savings Act Authored by New Mexico Democrat Sen. Martin Heinrich; promoted by Sen. Chuck Schumer Aimed at protecting ratepayers; described by Schumer as having “more teeth” than the Ratepayer Protection Act because the Ratepayer Protection Act’s protections are voluntary.

⚙️ Rising Infrastructure and Utility Costs

The rapid growth of data centers has significantly impacted regional energy grids and wholesale electricity costs:

  • Overall Ratepayer Impact: PJM, a regional transmission organization serving 13 states and the District of Columbia (including Northern Virginia), has an Independent Market Monitor estimating that data centers have cost their 67 million ratepayers approximately $29 billion over roughly the past two years.
  • State-Level Costs: Maryland customers pay an estimated $168 to $216 more per year on electricity bills primarily due to the data center boom.
  • Infrastructure Demands: Utilities are constructing new power lines, substations, and other grid-connecting infrastructure. Connor Waldoch, co-founder and chief strategy officer at Grid Status, notes, “We’re talking tens to hundreds of millions of dollars [of infrastructure] that are being built by these local utilities.”
  • Cost Recovery: Jeremy L. Slayton, a spokesman for Dominion Energy, which serves Loudoun County, Virginia, stated, “We recover costs for distribution and transmission infrastructure from customers.”

🧩 Challenges in Determining Consumer Impact

Calculating the precise cost passed on to residential ratepayers is difficult due to several variables and a lack of transparency:

  • Local Variables: According to Lucy Qiu, a professor at the School of Public Policy at the University of Maryland, consumer impact depends on utilities’ power-purchasing contracts, retail rates, regulatory decisions, the scale of upgrades, and how utilities share accounting.
  • Lack of Transparency: Ari Peskoe, director of the Harvard Electricity Law Initiative, states that a “single, clean number” for nationwide data center costs is impossible because much of the data regarding what data centers pay is hidden behind non-disclosure agreements (NDAs).
  • Prevalence of NDAs: A study by the University of Mary Washington found that NDAs had been signed in 80% of Virginia localities where there were existing, approved, or proposed data centers.

💡 Political Ramifications

The issue of data center growth and energy costs has also entered political campaigns. Ohio Republican Sen. Jon Husted is currently in a heated reelection campaign against Democrat Sherrod Brown, who lost his Senate seat in 2024. Brown has made Husted’s past support of data centers in Ohio a major campaign issue.

#AIdatacenters #EnergyPolicy #RatepayerProtection #GridInfrastructure

Source: Data centers

item.title: Amazon Urges Support for AI Data Centers Warning of Geopolitical Risks
item.description:
Amazon Urges Support for AI Data Centers Warning of Geopolitical Risks

Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Gorman has published a blog post calling for public support of AI data center projects, warning that blocking them could cause irreparable harm to the US economy and national security. The publication comes as public support for data centers has plummeted, with communities across the United States raising concerns about jobs, environmental impact, power demands, and AI safety.

🔍 Overview

The push from Amazon comes amid rising local backlash and over 100 data center moratoriums currently being considered across the country. AWS CEO Matt Gorman warned that the United States cannot afford to lose the geopolitical race for AI dominance, stating that enacting these moratoriums would write a “losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations.” Gorman also argued that some public opposition is fueled by myths, social media, 24/7 news, and reports of foreign nations intentionally seeding misinformation in the US to trick communities into slowing down the build-out.

⚙️ Key details

To address local friction and establish clearer practices, Amazon is codifying several measures under a new “Data Center Commitment.” Additionally, the company has altered how it interacts with local government agencies:

  • Community Investment: Amazon has pledged to invest more than $1 billion to support communities neighboring its data centers.
  • Economic and Utility Safeguards: The commitment includes practices around creating jobs and preventing increases to local energy rates.
  • Elimination of NDAs: Amazon will no longer use nondisclosure agreements with government agencies. This policy change follows a probe by Democratic lawmaker Jamie Raskin into tech companies’ secret deals with local officials.
  • Shift toward Transparency: Commenting on the change, Amazon chief global affairs and legal officer David Zapolsky noted that while the industry has a history of secrecy, “it just didn’t make sense” to continue requiring NDAs when community leaders need to share information with constituents.

#AWS #DataCenters #Infrastructure #Amazon

Source: Amazon writes scary blog warning communities not to block data centers

item.title: California passes bills to force data‑center energy and water disclosures
item.description:
California passes bills to force data‑center energy and water disclosures

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed seven bills on Monday that aim to increase transparency around data centers’ electricity and water consumption.

🔍 Overview

  • Data centers are expanding across the U.S., prompting protests over potential strain on power grids and local water supplies.
  • The new California legislation seeks to give communities better data and more say on how data centers impact electricity bills and water supply.

🧩 Legislative Details

Bill Requirement
SB 886, SB 1168, AB 2383 Direct the California Public Utilities Commission to create separate power rates for data centers to recoup grid‑connection costs
AB 1577 Requires monthly reporting on data centers’ energy consumption
AB 2619, AB 2469 Require water‑use disclosures; AB 2469 also makes operators cover infrastructure‑upgrade costs
SB 887 Removes categorical exemptions from the California Environmental Quality Act, ensuring data centers undergo environmental review

⚙️ Why it matters

  • Without clear data, scientists have found it “extremely frustrating to try to understand basic information,” says Mark Specht, senior manager for the climate and energy program at the Union of Concerned Scientists.
  • The disclosure rules begin next year but still won’t provide a full picture of consumption.
  • Two possible outcomes are outlined: (1) ballooning electricity demand could lead to costly new infrastructure that may be overbuilt if AI demand falls, passing costs to other consumers; (2) spreading fixed grid‑maintenance costs across more customers could lower electricity rates, but this depends on data centers contributing to distribution‑system costs rather than only connecting to high‑voltage transmission.
  • Water‑use data remain opaque; water providers have refused to share usage figures, and current disclosures only apply when seeking permits or business licenses, leaving year‑to‑year usage unclear.

📊 Perspectives

  • “I’m happy [AB 1577] passed,” Specht said, noting the difficulty in researching state offers.
  • “I wouldn’t say definitively that data centers have increased the cost [of electricity],” he added, acknowledging the lack of numbers to demonstrate either increase or potential savings.
  • As data centers’ power needs grow, monitoring their energy and water consumption becomes increasingly important.

#California #DataCenters #EnergyPolicy #WaterUse

Source: Data centers are black boxes, but California wants to change that

item.title: Survey Finds Majority of Likely Voters Oppose AI Data Center Construction
item.description:
Survey Finds Majority of Likely Voters Oppose AI Data Center Construction

A survey of 1,503 likely voters conducted in early September reveals that 61 percent of respondents oppose the construction of data centers used to power AI technology, while 14 percent say they strongly support it.

⚙️ Key details

Opposition to AI data centers varies by political affiliation and voter demographic:

  • Donald Trump voters: Split nearly evenly with 49 percent support and 45 percent oppose.
  • Kamala Harris voters: 74 percent lean oppose.
  • Non-voters: 67 percent lean oppose.
  • Age demographics: AI and data centers registered at less than 1 percent for most demographics, except for the 18–29 group, where 3 percent selected this issue over other popular responses such as inflation, foreign policy, and the economy.

Among those who oppose the construction of data centers, 56 percent support limits, while 38 percent prefer a total ban.

💡 Why it matters

Respondents cited several specific reasons for their opposition:

Reason for Opposition Percentage
Environment/water usage 32%
Impact on local communities 21%
General distrust or dislike of AI 18%
Regulation concerns 10%
The economy 9%

Regarding trust in handling the issue, 40 percent of 554 respondents favored Democrats and 42 percent favored Republicans, while 18 percent refused or did not know. This follows previous polling, including a March NBC News poll where AI polled lower than ICE, and a May Gallup poll showing seven in ten Americans opposed local construction of AI data centers.

#AI #DataCenters #PublicOpinion #Infrastructure

Source: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll
